shrines.label: Gorakh Dibbi · Rudra Kund
shrines.evidence: The Kangra temple authority records the kund beside the main temple and its ten-step approach.
shrines.notes: The bubbling cold-water kund is associated with Guru Gorakhnath. The modeled stone basin follows the documented form.
shrines.tradition: Nath tradition • Guru Gorakhnath and the Rudra Kund

shrines.label: Radha–Krishna Temple
shrines.evidence: The Kangra temple authority places the Radha–Krishna temple by Gorakh Dibbi.
shrines.notes: A Vaishnava shrine on the adjacent terrace. The figures are iconographic studies of Radha and flute-bearing Krishna.
shrines.tradition: Vaishnava tradition • Radha and Krishna

shrines.label: Shiva–Shakti · Linga and Jyoti
shrines.evidence: The Kangra temple authority describes a linga and flame at the head of about fifteen steps immediately above Gorakh Dibbi.
shrines.notes: The upper shrine models the documented sacred forms. Its exact room dimensions and installed surfaces remain approximate.
shrines.tradition: Shaiva and Shakta traditions • The linga with a Jyoti

shrines.label: Seja Bhawan · Devi’s Resting Chamber
shrines.evidence: The temple’s gallery identifies the domed Seja Bhawan. The Shaiyan Aarti page documents its use.
shrines.notes: The second part of the bedtime aarti takes place here, with verses from Adi Shankaracharya’s Saundarya Lahari.
shrines.tradition: Shakta tradition • Shaiyan Aarti and Saundarya Lahari

shrines.label: Charan Paduka · Sacred Footprints
shrines.evidence: The temple gallery shows the paired metal footprints at the entrance.
shrines.notes: The paired footprints represent the Devi’s presence. The modeled paduka follows the photographed metal plate and floral offerings.
shrines.tradition: Shakta tradition • Reverence for the Devi’s footprints

shrines.label: Yogini Kund
shrines.evidence: The Kangra temple authority places the ritual kund near the main entrance.
shrines.notes: Khappar Puja is documented here. The basin and its exact position are modeled approximately.
shrines.tradition: Shakta ritual • Khappar Puja at the Yogini Kund

shrines.label: Akbar’s Chhatra
shrines.evidence: A documented devotional offering with a published photograph of the display.
shrines.notes: The metal parasol is associated with Akbar in temple tradition. The canopy is modeled from its photographed concentric bands.
shrines.tradition: Offering tradition • The story of Akbar’s chhatra

shrines.label: Kharak Singh’s Silver Door
shrines.evidence: The 1872–73 archaeological field report attributes the silver folding door to Kharak Singh.
shrines.notes: The threshold models the open folding leaves and silver floral decoration. Individual repousse patterns are approximate.
shrines.tradition: Temple patronage • Kharak Singh’s silver-plated door

shrines.label: Jawala Ji · Checkered Courtyard
shrines.evidence: The temple gallery and aerial photographs show the court and its two distinct gilded roofs.
shrines.notes: The court connects the Paduka, main temple, the three visible domed pavilions and Seja Bhawan.
shrines.tradition: Main compound • Pilgrim entrance and darshan routes

shrines.label: Sharada Peeth · Roofless Sanctuary
shrines.evidence: The survey records a 3.8 m square chamber on a raised plinth with a west door.
shrines.notes: Sacred tradition links Sharada with learning and Adi Shankaracharya’s ascent to the Sarvajna Peetha. The original worshipped form remains unverified.
shrines.tradition: Sharada / Saraswati • Shakti Peetha and Sarvajna Peetha traditions

shrines.label: Western Stone Stairway
shrines.evidence: The field report counts 63 treads. The site plan shows the stair west of the terrace.
shrines.notes: Stepped stone flanking walls rise with the stair to the entrance podium.
shrines.tradition: Historical approach • Western stone ascent

shrines.label: West Gateway · Double Porch Remains
shrines.evidence: The survey describes a two-part porch with the southern half largely lost.
shrines.notes: The surviving northern side preserves pilasters and panel remnants.
shrines.tradition: Kashmiri stone architecture • Ruined double porch

shrines.label: West Wall · Taqchah A
shrines.evidence: A recess just north of the portal is marked Niche A on the field plan.
shrines.notes: A taqchah is a wall niche. The original occupant of this recess is uncertain.
shrines.tradition: Enclosure niche • Original use uncertain

shrines.label: North Wall · Taqchah B
shrines.evidence: The north niche is documented in the middle of the wall.
shrines.notes: Stein reported two small lingas in this chamber. The model depicts the surviving recess.
shrines.tradition: Enclosure niche • Two small lingas recorded historically

shrines.label: East Wall · Taqchah C
shrines.evidence: The field plan marks a recessed niche north of the east postern.
shrines.notes: Its crowning elements are missing. The model shows the surviving lower courses.
shrines.tradition: Enclosure niche • Upper courses lost

shrines.label: Eastern Postern
shrines.evidence: The field survey describes a simple lintelled doorway with a narrower outer end.
shrines.notes: The route stops inside the enclosure at the debris-filled threshold.
shrines.tradition: Historical feature • Lintelled eastern doorway

shrines.label: Sanctuary · East Trefoil Relief
shrines.evidence: The survey records blind trefoil recesses within nested pediments on three sanctuary faces.
shrines.notes: This stone relief is modeled from the recorded motif and serves as a view of the east face.
shrines.tradition: Kashmiri stone architecture • Blind trefoil and pediments
